 Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders 
 He’s still No. 2. Coming into the Cleveland Browns ‘ big Week 8 game against the Steelers in Pittsburgh, with supremacy in the AFC North on the line, there were significant questions about how the Browns’ quarterback depth chart would shape up behind starter Deshaun Watson . There were rumblings that the Browns had been giving a long look at Dillon Gabriel , now off the injured reserve, as the No. 2 quarterback on the team’s list, supplanting Shedeur Sanders . That would have been a remarkable turn of events for a Browns team that has played Sanders only one NFL snap this season. 
 But on Sunday, not long before kickoff in Pittsburgh, the team made its final announcement: Yes, Sanders is still No. 2, with Gabriel registering as inactive, but the emergency No.3 quarterback and Taylen Green inactive altogether.
 Tytus Howard , the starting right tackle, officially cleared protocol. 
 As Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports: “Howard clearing concussion protocol was the biggest pregame status news. Gabriel the emergency QB in his first game on the active roster.”
 Howard clearing concussion protocol was the biggest pregame status news. Gabriel the emergency QB in his first game on the active roster. https://t.co/tuLMb8O5QK — Zac Jackson (@AkronJackson) November 1, 2026 
 Browns Not Trading Shedeur Sanders
 There was some relevance to this decision early in the game against the Steelers, too, as Sanders had to take the field after Deshaun Watson took a shot to the head on the team’s first drive. Sanders was 2-for-2 passing in his first time out, but for only two yards. Watson returned the following series.
 Throughout the week coming into this game, the Browns had questions in their quarterback room. Watson has obviously secured his status as the starter in Cleveland, but there was remaining confusion about what the team would do with the rest of its QB crew. Reports persisted that Sanders would remain the QB2, but eyebrows were raised, certainly, when coach Todd Monken appeared to be uncertain of his depth chart himself. 
 Asked last Monday about how Gabriel coming off the injured reserve–he’d been stashed on IR for the first seven weeks with a back injury–would affect the QB room, Monken said, “I haven’t gotten there yet.” 
 And as for possibly trading either Gabriel, who started six games last year, or Sanders, who started seven, the word from team insiders continues to be that it’s not happening. 
 From Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com : “They have no plans to trade Sanders or Gabriel before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, unless someone makes them an offer they can’t refuse. As of now, they’re not shopping any of their QBs.”
